accepted.name: photoobj_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  run,
  rerun,
  field,
  mode,
  type,
  clean,
  flags,
  rowc,
  colc,
  cmodelmag_u,
  cmodelmag_g,
  cmodelmag_r,
  u,
  g,
  r,
  i,
  z,
  ra,
  dec,
  b,
  l,
  extinction_r,
  mjd,
  loadversion
FROM photoobj
accepted.description: One-row-per-photometric-object projection with core identifiers, sky coordinates, photometric magnitudes and basic quality flags. Use this to select cohorts of photometric objects or as the base input for joins and aggregations. | Use for: Select photometric objects by position, magnitude or quality flag; Join photometry to spectroscopy or neighbors; Compute distributions/aggregates of magnitudes or colors

accepted.name: photo_type_lookup
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  value,
  name,
  description
FROM photo_type
accepted.description: Canonical projection of the photo_type lookup table (one row per type value). Use this to map photoobj.type codes to human-readable names and descriptions when normalizing results. | Use for: Explain type codes associated with photometric objects; Join photometry to type names for reporting or filtering

accepted.name: specobj_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobjid,
  bestobjid,
  plateid,
  scienceprimary,
  segue2primary,
  survey,
  programname,
  mjd,
  plate,
  fiberid,
  special_target1,
  segue2_target1,
  segue2_target2,
  ancillary_target1,
  ra,
  dec,
  z,
  zerr,
  zwarning,
  class,
  subclass,
  veldisp,
  veldisperr,
  loadversion
FROM specobj
accepted.description: One-row-per-spectroscopic-object projection with identifiers, linking to photometric object via bestobjid, sky coordinates, redshift and classification fields. Use as the canonical spectroscopic row for joins and filtering. | Use for: Link spectroscopy to photometry via bestobjid; Select spectroscopic targets by redshift, class or quality flags; Aggregate spectroscopic measures by program or plate

accepted.name: specobj_with_photo
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.plateid,
  s.scienceprimary,
  s.survey,
  s.programname,
  s.mjd AS mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid,
  s.ra AS ra,
  s.dec AS dec,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.zwarning,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode AS mode,
  p.type AS type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z AS z_mag,
  p.extinction_r
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
accepted.description: Denormalized join of specobj to its matched photometric best object (photoobj) including spectroscopic redshift and photometric magnitudes. Use this when combining spectroscopic properties with photometry for the same object. | Use for: Compare photometry and spectroscopy for the same targets; Filter spectroscopic samples by photometric colors or quality; Compute color vs redshift trends

accepted.name: neighbors_per_obj
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  COUNT(neighborobjid) AS neighbor_count,
  MIN(distance) AS min_distance,
  AVG(distance) AS avg_distance
FROM neighbors
GROUP BY objid
accepted.description: Aggregated neighbor statistics per objid: total neighbor count, minimum distance to any neighbor, and average neighbor distance. Use to quantify local crowding or nearest-neighbor distance distributions. | Use for: Find isolated objects (large min_distance or zero neighbors); Rank objects by neighbor density; Join neighbor density to photometry or spectroscopy

accepted.name: photoobj_color_indices
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  u,
  g,
  r,
  i,
  z,
  (u - g) AS u_minus_g,
  (g - r) AS g_minus_r,
  (r - i) AS r_minus_i,
  (i - z) AS i_minus_z,
  (cmodelmag_u - cmodelmag_r) AS cmodel_u_minus_r
FROM photoobj
accepted.description: Per-object derived photometric color indices and a simple magnitude summary. Useful for color-based selection or for feeding into ranking/aggregation pipelines. | Use for: Color selection (e.g., select objects in color boxes); Compute color distributions or color-color diagrams; Combine colors with spectroscopy for population studies

accepted.name: photo_neighbors_join
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode,
  p1.ra AS ra,
  p1.dec AS dec,
  p1.u AS u,
  p1.g AS g,
  p1.r AS r,
  p1.i AS i,
  p1.z AS z,
  p2.ra AS neighbor_ra,
  p2.dec AS neighbor_dec,
  p2.u AS neighbor_u,
  p2.g AS neighbor_g,
  p2.r AS neighbor_r,
  p2.i AS neighbor_i,
  p2.z AS neighbor_z
FROM neighbors n
LEFT JOIN photoobj p1
  ON n.objid = p1.objid
LEFT JOIN photoobj p2
  ON n.neighborobjid = p2.objid
accepted.description: Explode neighbor edges by joining neighbors to the photometric attributes of both endpoints. Each row is one neighbor relationship with photometry for objid and neighborobjid. Useful when analyzing pair properties or computing pairwise differences. | Use for: Compute photometric differences between neighboring objects; Filter neighbor pairs by type or distance; Aggregate pair statistics (e.g., average magnitude difference vs distance)

accepted.name: specobj_latest_per_bestobj
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobjid,
  bestobjid,
  plateid,
  scienceprimary,
  mjd,
  loadversion,
  z,
  zerr,
  zwarning,
  class,
  subclass,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY bestobjid ORDER BY COALESCE(mjd, -1) DESC, COALESCE(loadversion, -1) DESC, specobjid) AS spec_rank
FROM specobj
accepted.description: For each bestobjid (photometric object), rank associated spectroscopic records by mjd and loadversion to produce a deterministic latest-per-bestobj view. Exposes a rank so callers can select top-N per bestobjid. | Use for: Select the most recent spectrum for each photometric object; Resolve duplicate spectroscopic records per photometric match; Create top-N spectroscopic samples per object

accepted.name: photoobj_running_counts_by_field
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  objid,
  run,
  field,
  objid AS ordering_objid,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY field ORDER BY objid ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_count_in_field
FROM photoobj
accepted.description: Per-photoobj running count within each field ordered by objid. Exposes a running_total so callers can compute densities or percentile positions within a field. | Use for: Compute per-field cumulative distributions or percentiles; Identify objects by rank order within a field

accepted.name: galspecline_exists
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobjid,
  1 AS has_galspecline
FROM galspecline
accepted.description: Simple presence flag for specobjid indicating whether a galspecline row exists. Useful to join to specobj to quickly filter or label spectra that have associated galspecline products. | Use for: Flag spectra that have additional derived products; Join to specobj to restrict to spectra with galspecline
